c3aa9fd6f8.q: How did MongoDB's sales operations structure evolve from $100 million to $2 billion in revenue?
c3aa9fd6f8.a: At $100 million, MongoDB's sales operations consisted of Meghan Gill, one analyst, and a couple of Salesforce folks managing 60-70 reps. By the time the company reached $2 billion as a public company with 600-700 reps, sales operations evolved into specialized pillars: a field operations team sitting close to each sales leader by geography, a planning and compensation team, and a team focused on systems, process, analytics, and reporting.

c3aa9fd6f8.rq: Planning became basically a full year process. In Q1 you're issuing all the new plans, in Q2 you're starting to think about changes, by Q3 you're doing bottom-up planning, and Q4 is all about systems and implementation.

7ca4f43bdc.q: What is the Smoke Report tool and how does MongoDB use it for territory planning?
7ca4f43bdc.a: The Smoke Report is a tool MongoDB built to show engagement data from both internal and external systems, based on the concept of 'where there's smoke, there's fire' for detecting adoption signals of their open source database. Over time, MongoDB built an internal tool on MongoDB itself to enable leaders to see all different data points and change territories dynamically, with field ops partners helping build territories using this tooling.

1f20465b56.q: What is the TAM-based territory allocation method that MongoDB used for sales rep assignments?
1f20465b56.a: MongoDB used a concept called Total Addressable Market (TAM) to quantify the value of each account and give each rep an equal amount of TAM, ensuring they had an equal shot at hitting their number. This approach helped identify whether a rep had enough accounts to work with or conversely had more than they could possibly prospect into, creating fair territory divisions across the sales team.

11574418e5.q: What is the difference between Sales Operations and Revenue Operations according to Meghan Gill?
11574418e5.a: Revenue Operations brings together all operations functions—sales, marketing, customer success, and services—into one function aligned on the same metrics for cross-functional collaboration. Gill takes a contrarian view, arguing that while this works for early-stage startups with resource constraints, as companies scale, operations teams should be close to the business, with a balance between centralized functions and field-close teams to avoid centralized functions becoming ineffective.

704a9a3a56.q: Why is data quality the biggest challenge in sales territory planning systems?
704a9a3a56.a: The hardest part of territory planning is getting the data right because nobody has a perfect CRM with perfectly scrubbed data. Keeping the database clean was always one of the biggest challenges MongoDB faced, as it directly fed into the tools built to divide territories evenly and enable leaders to manage account distribution.
